name: Plate Condenser
full_description: A plate condenser uses corrugated plate channels to condense vapor into liquid by transferring heat to cooling water, chilled water, glycol, air-assisted loops, or another coolant. The compact plate surface supports fast thermal response and high heat-transfer efficiency in evaporation systems, refrigeration systems, solvent recovery, chemical processes, power auxiliaries, marine service, and food or pharmaceutical utilities.
advantage: Large corrugated plate area supports high condensation heat-transfer coefficients.
Compact construction reduces installation footprint and refrigerant or vapor hold-up.
Fast thermal response helps systems follow changing vapor loads.
Openable, gasketed, semi-welded, or welded configurations can be selected by media and maintenance needs.
Material selection can address seawater, acidic vapor, refrigerants, solvents, and hygienic services.
Can be paired with plate evaporators, MVR systems, refrigeration units, and process heat-recovery loops.

technical_parameters.Materials: Stainless steel, titanium, duplex stainless steel, and corrosion-resistant alloys
technical_parameters.Configuration: Gasketed, semi-welded, fully welded, or plate-shell designs by service
technical_parameters.Cooling media: Cooling water, chilled water, glycol, seawater, or process coolant by duty
technical_parameters.Condensing side: Plate channels configured for vapor distribution and condensate drainage
technical_parameters.Typical applications: Evaporation systems, ammonia refrigeration, solvent recovery, chemical condensers, marine service, food and pharmaceutical utilities

details.title: Condensation duty
details.content: The exchanger should be sized around vapor composition, condensation curve, non-condensable gas, cooling medium temperature, pressure drop, and condensate drainage.

details.title: Configuration choice
details.content: Clean water vapor may use a gasketed arrangement, while refrigerants, solvents, corrosive vapor, or higher pressure may require semi-welded, welded, or plate-shell designs.
